Senses.PreferredTarget: an old woman's concern is pressing
AlternateTargets: old-woman concern pressed to the utmost
pressing concern like an old woman's
Senses.Explanation: The phrase appraises urgently solicitous intervention: records sometimes praise it and sometimes compare it to poisoned honey. Literally, "an old woman's concern is pressing": old woman or granny (老婆) plus the concern being urgent or pressed hard (心切). The phrase occurs 270 times in 129 allowlisted texts. It is a predicate applied to an unnamed interlocutor's insistent words or actions toward someone else, not the name of an inner state or a sentimental ideal. In the Linji–Huangbo–Dayu case, Dayu says Huangbo's old-woman concern was so pressing that "for you he exhausted himself completely" (為汝得徹困); when Linji returns, he says it was "only because the old-woman concern was pressing" (祇為老婆心切). In another exchange, a layman calls Huitang's concern pressing and Huitang replies, "I only want you to arrive home" (秖要公到家耳). The records thus show the idiom through predicates, agents, and replies rather than through a modern emotional gloss.
Senses.Note: The phrase is neither automatically praise nor a guarantee that the action described is harmless. A commentary reports that people call Jinniu's carrying rice and dancing "pressing old-woman concern," then rejects their reading: it is "arsenic soaked in honey to entice people to put it in their mouths" (以蜜浸砒霜誘人下口). Elsewhere the location of Yaoshan's pressing concern is itself made the next interview question: "where is the place of his pressing old-woman concern?" (那裏是他老婆心切處). It can also enter verse, as in "pressing old-woman concern, laughing ha-ha, letting bystanders say long or short" (老婆心切呵呵笑，一任傍人說短長). Common frames include "only because" (the “only because” form, 24 occurrences; variant 祇為, 7) and "so very" (得恁麼老婆心切, 18). These uses support a forceful relational appraisal while preserving the possibility of criticism.

Occurrences.Kwic: 愚曰：黃檗與麼老婆心切，為汝得徹困，更來這裡問有過無過？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (祖庭鉗鎚錄), the Linji Yixuan encounter with Gao'an Dayu. Gao'an Dayu is the exact speaker: after Linji reports Huangbo Xiyun's three beatings and asks whether he was at fault, Dayu says Huangbo was so earnestly grandmotherly for him.

Occurrences.Kwic: 檗見便問：這漢來來去去，有甚了期？師曰：祇為老婆心切。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (祖庭鉗鎚錄). On returning, Linji answers Huangbo's complaint about his coming and going: only because the old-woman concern was pressing. The exact headword-bearing actor is Linji Yixuan.

Occurrences.Kwic: 公釋然即拜之曰。和尚得恁麼老婆心切。堂笑曰。秖要公到家耳。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (續傳燈錄). Huang Tingjian is the exact named public utterer.

ActorAttribution.ReviewedBy: Codex lane-C second independent semantic repair
ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The grammar explicitly marks Huang Tingjian’s direct turn with 公…曰; he tells Huitang Zuxin that the master’s old-woman concern is exceedingly pressing, and Huitang replies.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：藥山老漢得恁老婆心切。進云：且那裏是他老婆心切處？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (列祖提綱錄) explicitly introduces Yu'an Zhiji's New Year's Eve informal address. Yu'an Zhiji is the exact speaker who comments that old Yaoshan was so earnestly grandmotherly in offering the monk a food-abstention formula.

Occurrences.Kwic: 人見其自舁飯作舞，多道老婆心切，殊不知以蜜浸砒霜誘人下口。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (香嚴禪師語錄). Puming is the exact actor: the commentator self-identifies as (普明) and rejects the common (金牛) reading.

Occurrences.Kwic: 老婆心切呵呵笑，一任傍人說短長。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (香嚴禪師語錄). Puming is the exact actor: he supplies the (趙州) verse (老婆心切呵呵笑).
